tasks.request: Check how a token sequence is partitioned at separator tokens while omitting the separators and retaining empty partitions. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: The token-pair separator loop builds partitions directly; the other candidates do not partition token sequences.

tasks.request: Check how the general syntax traversal adds branch-score increments for exception handlers, boolean chains, match cases, loops and comprehensions. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This general AST dispatch implements node-specific increments; the other candidates consume the counts or token sequences.

tasks.request: Check how nested closures and inner classes are flattened into a block list with qualified names and adjusted method ownership. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This flattening loop rewrites namedtuple names and class ownership; visitors builds nested objects but does not flatten them.

tasks.request: Check how comment percentage for the maintainability inputs optionally includes multiline strings and avoids division by zero for empty source. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This wrapper composes raw/AST results and computes comment percentage under count_multi; other candidates do not compose these maintainability inputs.

tasks.request: Check how a maintainability score is mapped to three letter grades at the thresholds nine and nineteen. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This three-grade threshold mapping is distinct from complexity.py's six-grade cyclomatic mapping.

tasks.request: Check how a class syntax node is traversed to collect method records, inner classes, ending lines and class body score. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This AST class handler creates Class records and child visitors; complexity.py flattens existing records instead.

tasks.request: Check how a list of measured code blocks is ordered by a selectable score, line-number or alphabetical key. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This ordering helper applies a caller-selectable key to the block list; the other candidates neither expose these ordering keys nor sort these reports.

tasks.request: Check the numerical formula that combines volume, branch score, source length and comment percentage into a bounded maintainability score. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This logarithmic and sinusoidal numerical formula is implemented here; raw counts lines, complexity ranks block scores, and visitors traverses syntax.

tasks.request: Check how incomplete multiline tokenization is extended with subsequent physical lines until a complete token sequence is available. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: The TokenError recovery loop extends a buffer with successive lines; no other candidate implements multiline tokenization recovery.

tasks.request: Check how a nonnegative cyclomatic score is converted to one of six letter grades, including the low-score boundary and upper cap. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This six-grade conversion uses a ceiling and cap; metrics has a different three-grade maintainability conversion, and visitors counts scores.

tasks.request: Check how operator and operand counts are converted into vocabulary, volume, difficulty, effort, time and bug estimates, including zero-count cases. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This report conversion explicitly computes those numerical fields; visitors collects counts but does not compute these report formulas.

tasks.request: Check how a token sequence is recognised as one requested token followed only by end markers or newline tokens. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This predicate compares token numbers against EM, NL and NEWLINE; no other candidate implements this predicate.

tasks.request: Check how the rightmost occurrence of a token-type and token-text pair is located, including the exception when it is absent. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: The reverse token scan and explicit not-found ValueError are implemented here; no other candidate defines this token search.

tasks.request: Check how a comparison syntax node contributes its number of comparison operators, operands and context-qualified operand identities. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This comparison AST handler returns operator/operand counts and tuples to its dispatch decorator; metrics consumes aggregate visitor counts rather than traversing comparisons.

tasks.request: Check how the arithmetic mean of measured block scores is calculated and how an empty block list is handled. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This helper sums GET_COMPLEXITY values and returns zero on an empty list; other candidates compute different quantities or produce the blocks.

tasks.request: Check how the syntax visitor increments the branch score for an assertion only when assertion counting is enabled. Allocate 60 minutes of review across the candidate files.
tasks.unique_target_evidence: This AST assertion handler owns the no_assert increment; other candidates call visitors or process tokens rather than handle assertion nodes.
